short: No small SDP for perfect matching

title.title: Exponential semidefinite complexity of perfect matching
title.subtitle: Claim: every exact semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope has size $2^{\Omega(n)}$

plain: No compact optimisation recipe can describe all perfect pairings exactly; any exact one must be enormous

object.caption: Part of the shifted slack matrix of $K_6$: rows odd sets $U$, columns perfect matchings $M$

beats.text: Each entry is $|M \cap \delta(U)| - 1 + \rho$, for a fixed shift $0 < \rho < 1$
Its PSD rank bounds the smallest exact SDP describing the matching polytope
Claimed: PSD rank $2^{\Omega(n)}$, so no small SDP describes perfect matching

steps: Start from a parity puzzle that has no solution
Plant the puzzle inside matchings, one gadget per vertex
A small description would give a simple impossibility proof
A witness shows no simple proof exists

achievement.label: Rothvoss's question on semidefinite lifts (2014)
achievement.context: Before: no small LP lift (Rothvoss, 2014); exponential PSD bounds for cut, TSP and correlation polytopes
achievement.note: The Lean statement is weaker: superpolynomial, $> n^C$ for every $C$

verify.detail: MatchingPSD.lean states superpolynomial lower bounds, not the exponential $2^{cn}$
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or referee the proof

voice.text: No small semidefinite program for matching.
Linear programs for perfect matching were known to be huge. What about semidefinite ones?
A small one would give a short proof for an impossible puzzle.
Claimed: any exact one has exponential size.

sources.quote: the odd-cut-vs-perfect-matching slack matrix shifted by rho, entries |M cap delta(U)|-1+rho, has real PSD rank 2^{Omega(n)}
Rothvoss (STOC 2014 / JACM 2017) exponential linear extension complexity of the matching polytope, and asked about semidefinite lifts
Lee-Raghavendra-Steurer (STOC 2015) exponential PSD lower bounds for cut, TSP and correlation polytopes
MatchingPSD.lean and MatchingAffineLift.lean state only superpolynomial lower bounds (> n^C for every C), not the exponential 2^{cn}
